extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, humor writers, and joke writers/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short jokes and longer stories with effective punch lines and jab lines, including structural models (Greg Dean, Mike Lukas) and pacing/timing advice. Useful for writers/performers crafting setup, connector, jabs, and the final punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setup is the stage-setting that primes an expectation or obvious interpretation. A clear setup builds the 1st story / target assumption that the punch will later overturn. Anti-patterns: vague or unfocused setups that fail to create a single, strong expectation; overlong setups that lose audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaks the expectation with surprise; climactic conclusion of a story or joke — a short line that gives a humorous reveal. The pivot on which the joke text turns — signals shift between semantic scripts needed to interpret the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be short, decisive, and reveal the reinterpretation. Place the punch so it functions as a stopping point; avoid explaining the joke. Anti-patterns: overlong punchlines, explanatory tags that kill the surprise, or a punch that doesn't create a clear reinterpretation of the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional follow-up that extends the punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tags to squeeze additional laughs after the punch without undoing the original surprise. Tags should build on the punch's reinterpretation rather than re-explain it. Excessive tagging can dilute the impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jab Line
rubrics_metrics.description: A funny line during the body of a story; functionally identical to a punch line but positioned anywhere in the text. Jabs build humorous tension, set comic pace and rhythm, and multiple jabs can precede the final punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use jabs to pace the journey and keep momentum; they create expectations and mini-reversals that lead toward the final punch. Anti-patterns: jabs that derail the narrative, break rhythm, or undercut the final punch's surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch placement / timing (punch at the end)
rubrics_metrics.description: The punch goes at the end: audience laughs after the surprise and the punch functions as a 'stopping point' structurally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the punch where it will not be spoken past; talking over or past the laugh wastes laughs. Timing is crucial — the punch should allow the audience to react before continuing. Anti-patterns: continuing the story through the laugh or moving the punch earlier so it loses its stopping-point power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greg Dean joke structure (five mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1st Story — the obvious/expected interpretation set up; Target Assumption — what audience assumes about the connector; Connector — the magical element with two interpretations; Reinterpretation — the alternative meaning revealed by the punch; 2nd Story — the new story implied by the punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the joke establishes a clear 1st story and target assumption, provides a connector with dual meanings, then delivers a reinterpretation that creates a coherent 2nd story. This model helps diagnose where a joke fails (e.g., missing a clear connector or a weak reinterpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mike Lukas: Premise / Setup / Punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise: the broad topic/observation underlying the joke. Setup: specific stage-setting that primes expectation. Punchline: the surprise that breaks the setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the premise (big-picture idea) from the setup (the immediate expectation) and ensure the punchline pivots the setup. Use the premise to generate multiple setups and jabs; test setups against the premise for thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can the joke be stated as setup → connector → punch?
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagnostic criterion: the joke should be expressible as setup → connector → punch (i.e., the connective element that supports two interpretations and allows the reinterpretation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can reduce the joke to that chain, the structure is likely sound. Use this as a quick test: identify the setup, find the connector with dual readings, and confirm the punch provides the reinterpretation. If you can't, the joke may need reframing or stronger connectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rubric checklist (5 questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Is there a clear setup (expectation building)? 2. Is there a clear punch (expectation breaking)? 3. Is the punch at the end? 4. If there are jab lines, do they pace the journey? 5. Could you state the joke as setup → connector → punch?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this five-question checklist as a concise evaluation tool when editing or rehearsing material. Answering 'no' to any question identifies a specific area to revise (setup clarity, punch clarity, placement, jab pacing, or structural connector).
